To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the existence of a blowup solution and its stability are proved by using the reduction of the system to a finite dimensional problem and a topological method.
we construct a finite dimensional problem for the system and then we show that this finite dimensional problem has a nontrivial solution which is stable and has a blowup profile.
we have constructed stable blowup solutions of a system of nonlinear parabolic equations with exponential nonlinearity and no gradient structure in any dimension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the blowup behavior of a reaction-diffusive system whose nonlinearities are of exponential form and whose diffusion coefficients are constant.
the following questions: What are the blowup solutions of a system of reaction-diffusion equations with exponential nonlinearities? How many are there? Are they stable? How does the singularity form?
the following questions: (i) What are the possible blowup profiles for the system? (ii) What is the dimension of the blowup space? (iii) What is the stability property of blowup?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system admits a stable blowup profile which is a solution of the system and it has a unique blowup point.
the blowup solutions are stable and their singularity formation can be completely described.
we can prove the existence of a finite-dimensional manifold of solutions which are stable in the sense that the blowup parameters are constant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a reaction-diffusive system with exponential nonlinear terms, the blowup solutions are stable and the blowup profiles have the same asymptotic behavior as in the semilinear case.
we have developed a new method of analysis for parabolic systems with exponential nonlinearities and we have shown that the classical method is not applicable for the present system.
, in the reaction-diffusion systems without gradient structure, the blowup phenomenon and the blowup rate can be determined by the finite dimensional reduction of the original problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lack of gradient structure in the nonlinearities is not a major obstacle to obtain a complete description in the blowup analysis.
the lack of gradient structure does not prevent the existence of blowup solutions and that the classical methods based upon energy-type estimates are not necessary to construct them.
, for this system, the blowup is stable and its singularity formation is described by a finite dimensional system of ODEs.
